# Brief — keepsake

**Status:** FROZEN — control brief for S1a. Do not edit after scaffolding.
**Director:** Paper Studio, creative owner
**Frozen:** 2026-10-25
**Style id:** keepsake

This is a family archive film for my grandparents' 50th anniversary. It is not a
wedding. Ruth and Peter have been married for fifty years, and the film is a
record of the ordinary things that lasted: the table, the garden, the teapot,
the same two people in the same chairs. It will be watched once, at the table,
by their children and grandchildren.

## 1. Occasion and audience

A family archive film for my grandparents' 50th anniversary. The audience is the
family, in one room, after lunch. Not a wedding, not a public event, not a
party. Nobody outside the family will see it.

## 2. Story in one sentence

Fifty years of Sundays: the same table, the same garden, the same two people,
and the small things that outlasted everything else.

## 3. Cast and faces

No on-camera cast. Photographs and captions only. No talking heads, no narrator,
no hands arranging objects, no footage of the anniversary itself.

## 4. Shape and length

1:1 book pages. Eight spreads. 45 seconds. One idea per spread. The first spread
is the title, the last is a short close. The six in between are photographs with
dense captions.

## 5. Feeling

Warm, patient, unsentimental. It should feel like a family archive someone kept
in a cupboard, not like a film someone made to impress a room.

## 6. Anti-feeling

Never a wedding invitation. Never a slideshow. Never a memorial card. Never an
advert. If it starts to feel glossy, ceremonial or rushed, it has failed.

## 7. Material and palette

Warm off-white paper, dark ink, and one muted terracotta accent. A serif display
face for names and dates, a quiet text face for captions. Paper fibre at low
opacity. No gloss, no gold, no sparkles, no foil, no metallic sheen. At most four
colours in one frame.

## 8. Type and words

Serif display for the title, names and dates. A quiet serif or humanist sans for
captions. Dense captions: one or two full sentences per spread, 18 words maximum
per caption. No all-caps paragraphs. The monogram stays small and quiet. No text
over a face.

## 9. Motion and pace

Slow page turns, one per spread. Photographs stay still. No camera shake, no
push-in faster than four percent, no bounce or overshoot. The page turn should
take long enough that the caption can be read before it starts. If 1.2 s and
1.6 s both read as slow, show me both at check and I will pick.

## 10. Sound

No music. Room tone only: a clock, a kettle, a chair, a garden. Silence is
allowed, and preferred on the first and last spread. No voice-over.

## 11. Refusals

No gloss, no gold, no sparkles, no foil, no wedding stationery, no stock-photo
smiles, no fast cuts, no more than four colours in a frame, no on-camera cast,
no music. Out of scope: weddings, memorials, birthdays and corporate work.

## 12. Tier and proof

Classic tier. We will know it worked if the family recognises the ordinary
details before they recognise themselves. It must feel like a family archive,
never like a wedding invitation or a slideshow. Proof: one title spread, one
caption-heavy spread and one close, all at 1:1, checked on a 390 px phone and at
45 seconds.
